final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is valid as far as it goes: the record does not support clean compliance, and monitoring/rollback are only supplementary controls. But the narrower caveated-compliance position still depends on a missing predicate that remains unresolved on the admissible record: evidence that the required pre-launch model-card disclosure actually exists, or alternatively that the exposed use case is excluded or covered by approved risk acceptance. Because none of those predicates is proven, the certification claim remains inadequately supported under the stated policy. This is not a downgrade based on business urgency or tone; it is a preservation of the original concern because the core evidentiary gap was not cured.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the final pre-launch model card actually contains the required merchant dispute support limitation disclosure.
No admissible evidence shows merchant dispute support is excluded from the initial rollout cohort.
No admissible evidence shows a reviewed and approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed merchant dispute support segment.
The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not substitute for disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The Actor's narrowed position is better framed, but it still rests on an unresolved compliance predicate: proof that required pre-launch disclosure is present in the launch artifact.
